overview: IIM Calcutta Innovation Park (IIMCIP) is a national, leading social-impact incubator established in 2014 under the aegis of IIM Calcutta. It is committed to building an inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem across India, with a focus on underserved regions, rural women entrepreneurs, and social impact-driven ventures. IIMCIP offers a range of programs including incubation, pre-incubation, acceleration, and specialized initiatives like MeitY TIDE 2.0, NIDHI-EIR, and Prakriti Incubation, providing mentorship, seed funding, market access, and networking opportunities to early-stage startups.
geographic_scope: Pan-India with special focus on East, North-East, and underserved regions
objectives: Develop an entrepreneurship ecosystem by addressing ecosystem gaps in underserved regions
Catalyze innovation and nurture startups by empowering entrepreneurs with innovative ideas
Enable women entrepreneurs by championing inclusiveness in the entrepreneurial ecosystem
Support early-stage startups through mentorship, capacity building, and access to funding
Facilitate product-market fit and scalability through structured incubation and acceleration programs
Promote socially transformative businesses that generate livelihoods and inclusive growth
Strengthen regional entrepreneurship ecosystems through government and corporate partnerships
Impact one billion lives globally by 2047 through innovation and entrepreneurship
eligibility: Eligibility varies by program. Generally, applicants must be Indian citizens with a startup registered in India or having an office in India. For specific programs: MeitY TIDE 2.0 requires ICT-enabled ideas solving national priority concerns; Prakriti Incubation targets early-stage, early-revenue, MVP startups from the North East Region in sustainability and circular economy; NIDHI-EIR requires applicants to be Indian citizens with minimum 4 years of formal education, first-generation innovators willing to work full-time on a technology business idea; Maruti Suzuki NURTURE welcomes early-stage startups with prototype/MVP in mobility, manufacturing, and social impact domains; Pragati Accelerator targets early revenue stage innovative technology-enabled social ventures from East & North-east India with scalable models.
benefits: Benefits include mentorship from industry experts and IIM Calcutta faculty/alumni, access to fully-furnished workspace at IIM Calcutta campus (free of charge), seed capital and investor connect opportunities, legal/secretarial/IT/HR support at preferential rates, capacity-building workshops, market access and networking opportunities, participation in demo days and pitch events, fellowship grants (e.g., Rs 4-7 lakhs for MeitY TIDE 2.0, Rs 15 lakhs reward grant for Prakriti top performers), equity consideration (up to 5% by IIMCIP), and access to corporate and government partnerships. Some programs offer cash rewards (e.g., Rs 13 lakhs in Maruti Suzuki NURTURE) and opportunities for paid Proof of Concept projects.
financial_support: Financial support varies across programs. IIMCIP provides seed capital through equity or debt instruments for early-stage ventures. Specific programs offer: MeitY TIDE 2.0 Entrepreneur-in-Residence: Rs 4 lakhs grant for validation and development; MeitY TIDE 2.0 Grant: Rs 7 lakhs for MVP development from PoC; NIDHI-EIR: Rs 30,000 per month fellowship for 12 months; Prakriti Incubation: Fellowship grant plus reward grant up to Rs 15 lakhs for top performers; Maruti Suzuki NURTURE: Cash rewards worth INR 13 lakhs and paid PoC opportunities; Pragati Accelerator: Upto Rs 10 lakhs award to top 3-5 startups; DST NIDHI-SSS: Average seed fund of Rs 25 lakhs, up to Rs 100 lakhs per startup via loan, equity, or equity-linked instruments at 2-3% interest. IIMCIP has till date provided seed funding support amounting to Rs.26 crores and facilitated follow-on funding of Rs.1,946 crores for incubated startups.
application_process: 1. Submit a formal application including business plan and expression of interest in joining the portfolio. 2. Application undergoes initial screening by IIMCIP management team. 3. Shortlisted candidates proceed to final review by an independent investment committee. 4. Upon approval, sign an incubation agreement with IIMCIP (requires registration as a for-profit company before signing). 5. Gain access to IIMCIP facilities and resources. 6. Work closely with assigned mentors through regular interactions. 7. Submit monthly progress updates and detailed quarterly reports for monitoring. 8. Graduate upon achieving self-sustainability, securing expansion funding, completing an acquisition, or reaching end of incubation term (standard period: 24 months). 9. IIMCIP may take up to 5% equity as consideration for incubation support.
required_documents: Proof of prototype or minimum viable product (MVP)
deadlines: Varies by program: Maruti Suzuki NURTURE Cohort 4 deadline is June 30, 2026; Prakriti Incubation Cohort 2 last date extended to July 31, 2026; MeitY TIDE 2.0 EiR: Last date for applications August 25, 2025; MeitY TIDE 2.0 Grant: Last date for applications January 5, 2026; NIDHI-EIR: Last date for applications August 10, 2024; Pragati Accelerator (2022): Last date for applications July 10, 2022; Balmer Lawrie National Level Startup Hunt: Last date for applications May 20, 2023. Some programs operate on rolling basis.
